content.line: This parasite is actually a crustacean called Cymothoa. And it starts out its life cycle on the gills, the external gills of the fish. Now all individuals are males to begin with. The first one to reach the gills of those fish becomes the female.

content.speaker: PERSON_4
content.line: She then mates with all the males and continues into the fish's mouth. It then sends your kids out of the room, sucks the fish's tongue dry until the tongue shrivels up and is gone, then it substitutes itself for the fish's tongue and keeps the fish alive and continuing to eat, while it stays there as the tongue, feeding off the fish's blood and mucus. Yo.

He incorporates vivid, continuous hand gestures to illustrate the parasite's actions and deliberately pauses for comedic effect before concluding with a colloquial interjection.

content.speaker: an unseen male narrator

content.speaker: PERSON_4
content.line: And you look at it and you say this is disgusting. And then you learn about what it was actually doing, and you know that it was worse than you thought. Because it ate the fish's tongue. Who does that?
content.description: [PERSON_4] concludes his commentary at a normal pace, his voice filled with a mix of humorous disbelief and shock. He gestures broadly and leans forward slightly to emphasize the bizarre and gruesome nature of the parasite's behavior.
